title: Impact of COVID-19 Restrictions on Singapore’s Economy and Robustness of National Stockpile of Essential Items
what_it_is: Impact of COVID-19 Restrictions on Singapore’s Economy and Robustness of National Stockpile of Essential Items

sections.label: Stockpile and COVID-19 questions
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Trade and Industry about national stockpile plans, public assurance, hoarding lessons, travel restrictions, economic impact and business measures.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what are the current plans in place for crises in terms of preparing for an adequate national stockpile and whether they are sufficiently robust; (b) how can the Government and the community work hand-in-hand to assure the public of adequate stockpiles; and (c) whether there are any lessons derived from the hoarding behaviour in the aftermath of raising the DORSCON level in February 2020.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry in view of the lockdown of countries during the current COVID-19 outbreak (a) how do the travel restrictions affect Singapore; (b) how will our economy be affected by the slowdown in movement of goods and supplies especially with the lockdown of Malaysia; and (c) what measures are in the pipeline to help affected businesses tide through this challenging period.

sections.label: Food strategy
sections.summary: For food, a strategy developed over many years combines stockpiling, import diversification and local production.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For food, we have a strategy developed over many years that entails a combination of stockpiling, import diversification and local production.

sections.label: Joint Ministerial Statement
sections.summary: Two weeks ago, Singapore and six other countries issued a Joint Ministerial Statement affirming commitment to supply chain connectivity for goods including essential supplies amidst COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Just two weeks ago, Singapore, together with Australia, Brunei Darussalam, Canada, Chile, Myanmar and New Zealand, issued a Joint Ministerial Statement affirming our collective commitment to ensuring supply chain connectivity to facilitate the flow of goods including essential supplies amidst the COVID-19 situation.

sections.label: Budgets and economic support
sections.summary: The Government has put forth about S$55 billion through the Unity and Resilience Budgets, and Deputy Prime Minister Heng will deliver a Ministerial Statement on additional support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The sharp fall in external demand, along with the plunge in tourist arrivals and cutback in domestic consumption are all expected to severely affect our economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Hence, the Government has so far put forth about S$55 billion through the Unity and Resilience Budgets to help Singaporeans, businesses and workers tide through this difficult period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In particular, the Resilience Budget has introduced and enhanced measures to protect jobs, help enterprises overcome immediate challenges and strengthen resilience for our economy and society to emerge stronger.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng will soon deliver a Ministerial Statement in Parliament on additional support for businesses and their workers, households and vulnerable groups, to better cope with the upcoming circuit breaker measures.

sections.label: Continuing multi-pronged strategy
sections.summary: Even when the outbreak recedes, Singapore must continue its multi-pronged strategy of stockpiling, import diversification and local production to remain resilient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Going forward, even when the outbreak recedes, we must continue to pursue our multi-pronged strategy of stockpiling, import diversification and local production to remain resilient.

sections.label: Personal Protective Equipment supply
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Minister can share what is being done to ensure sufficient Personal Protective Equipment for healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share what are we doing to ensure there is sufficient Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for healthcare workers?

sections.label: Mask production type and capacity
sections.summary: Asks what type of masks are produced, the daily capacity, and how self-sufficient Singapore is.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: If so, what is the type of masks being produced and the capacity a day, and how self-sufficient are we?

sections.label: Measures to keep basic goods stable
sections.summary: Asks what measures are in place to keep the cost of basic goods stable.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Fourth, thanks for reassuring us on food supply, but what are the measures that you have in place to keep the cost of basic goods stable?

sections.label: Prioritising masks for frontline workers
sections.summary: States surgical masks and hospital-grade equipment will continue to be prioritised for frontline workers, with reusable cloth masks issued to the general public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The second point, in response to Miss Cheng's question, is that yes, we will continue to prioritise the surgical masks and the hospital-grade equipment for our frontline workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This has been our stance from the beginning and we will continue to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is also the reason why we have issued the reusable cloth mask for the general public because the needs for the general public are quite different from the needs of the frontline healthcare workers, and we will continue to preserve our stockpile of hospital-grade PPE for our healthcare workers.
